insight: A little recent rain (2.6 mm) may be carrying some runoff to the shoreline — a modest upward pressure on bacteria. The model's main signals right now: high tide timing is lowering risk — how long before mid-morning the last high tide fell, which sets how much the water has just washed off the upper beach; high tide level is lowering risk — a high tide can mobilize bacteria held in wet sand and push the waterline toward outfalls; and 2.6 mm of rain has fallen, washing bacteria-laden runoff into the surf. The most recent sample, 3 days ago, was over the limit at 24000 MPN/100mL, and bacteria tend to linger from one sample to the next.
